channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Lula afirma năo ter preferęncia entre países e quer construir parcerias em minerais críticos
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), running for reelection, stated this Saturday, the 22nd, that Brazil is open to building partnerships with various countries in the critical minerals sector, without showing preference among nations. The statement reinforces the government's interest in expanding international cooperation in this strategic area.

item.title: Toffoli fecha as portas para mais um habeas corpus que tentava soltar Bolsonaro
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Dias Toffoli rejected another appeal (agravo regimental) seeking to reopen a habeas corpus petition to free former President Jair Bolsonaro, who is serving a 27-year, three-month sentence for leading the attempted coup. Toffoli stated the case had already been sent back and that third parties cannot interfere in the defense, as Bolsonaro has officially appointed lawyers. The justice also denied requests to recuse other ministers from the coup case.

item.title: Vida de Lulinha na Espanha é “bem modesta”, diz Quaquá
item.description: Washington Quaquá, mayor of Maricá and PT vice-president, once again defended Fábio Luís Lula da Silva (Lulinha), describing his life in Spain as 'quite modest,' despite reports that the son of President Lula lives in a luxury condominium near Madrid with a high rent. The statement follows new information published by Metrópoles about the businessman's lifestyle abroad.

item.title: Em eventos de campanha no Rio, Lula promete reforço na segurança e Flávio propőe 'guerra' a facçőes
item.description: During campaign events in Rio de Janeiro, President Lula (PT) promised to strengthen public security by sending a constitutional amendment to recreate the Ministry of Public Security and bolster the Federal Police and Highway Police, in addition to expanding the imprisonment of criminal factions. Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), a presidential candidate, proposed declaring 'war' on 'narco-terrorists,' classifying groups like the Red Command and PCC as narco-terrorist organizations. Both also addressed topics such as education and social security in their events.

item.title: Os ex-BBBs mais ricos a se candidatarem nas eleições de 2026
item.description: Six former BBB contestants run in the 2026 elections. Vivian Amorim (Uniao Brasil/AM) leads with R$3.4 million in assets, followed by Adrilles Jorge (Uniao Brasil/SP) with R$540k. Lucas Penteado (SP) declares only R$1,200.

item.title: PT publica foto de comício de Lula em BH e provoca Flávio: 'Chora não'
item.description: The PT posted on X a photo of Lula at a rally in Belo Horizonte during Patrus Ananias' gubernatorial campaign launch, provoking Senator Flávio Bolsonaro with the phrase 'Chora não'. The move aims to bolster PT's presence in Minas Gerais and counter the PL.

item.title: Lula: escolha em 2026 é sobre quem quer vender as praias e quem quer o povo nelas
item.description: Lula launched his re-election campaign in Rio de Janeiro with a speech contrasting those who want to sell the beaches (privatization) with those who want the people in them (public management). He emphasizes valuing public space and popular access as the core of his platform.

item.title: No Rio, Lula promete Ministério da Segurança e tirar bandidos de territórios
item.description: Lula promised to create a Ministry of Public Security and remove criminals from territories dominated by organized crime during his first campaign event in Rio de Janeiro alongside Eduardo Paes. He defended his alliance with Paes and praised Ricardo Couto for political 'cleaning' in the state, while Paes linked organized crime in politics to PL candidates.

item.title: Zema defende nova reforma da Previdência e aumento da contribuição
item.description: Romeu Zema advocated for a new Social Security reform that increases contribution time based on life expectancy, aiming to prevent deficits and safeguard already acquired rights, especially for new workers.

item.title: Em jingle, Zema fala em 'acabar com PT', mostra ministros do STF na cadeia e Virgínia surpresa
item.description: Novo candidate Romeu Zema released a campaign jingle pledging to end the PT and depicting STF ministers in prison. The ad adopts an aggressive tone targeting both the party and the Supreme Court.

item.title: Lulinha e Dark Horse trazem PF e Mendonça para a disputa eleitoral
item.description: Federal Police investigations involving Lulinha (Lula's son) and financing of the "Dark Horse" film about Bolsonaro put Supreme Court Justice André Mendonça at the center of the 2026 election race. Lulinha faces three inquiries for alleged influence peddling and corruption at the Health Ministry, while PF probes a R$61 million transfer from Banco Master to the documentary. Datafolha poll shows Lula at 47% vs 43% for Flávio Bolsonaro in a hypothetical runoff, within the margin of error.

item.title: Zema lança jingle de forró com vídeo que mostra Lula e ministros presos
item.description: Romeu Zema released a forró campaign jingle and AI-generated animation depicting Lula and STF ministers as prisoners. The satirical video 'Untouchables' shows Gilmar Mendes, Dias Toffoli, and Alexandre de Moraes dancing in a jail cell, reinforcing criticism of the three branches of government. The piece ends with Zema wearing the presidential sash and receiving news of a police operation against Lula and his son.

item.title: Vice-presidente do PT minimiza luxos de Lulinha: "Pequeno empresário"
item.description: PT Vice-President Washington Quaquá downplayed the luxury of Lulinha’s Madrid condo, calling the rent typical for a small Brazilian businessman. He criticized the overuse of police investigations in politics and argued the scandal will have minimal impact on Lula’s campaign.

item.title: Zema chama João Campos de “intocável das bets” por reduzir imposto
item.description: Romeu Zema criticized João Campos for lowering the service tax on sports betting in Recife to 2%, calling him the 'untouchable of bets' and vowing to ban the industry if elected president. Campos justified the tax cut as necessary to prevent revenue loss to other cities.

item.title: Lobista diz em mensagem no celular que Lulinha marcou reunião de governador do MA no Planalto
item.description: Messages found by the Federal Police on lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger's phone indicate that Fábio Luís Lula da Silva, son of President Lula, allegedly scheduled a meeting at the Planalto Palace with Maranhão governor Carlos Brandão. According to the lobbyist, the meeting aimed to secure the release of federal works in the state. The case raises suspicions about the president's son's role in political bargaining for federal resources.

item.title: Promessa de petróleo na foz do Amazonas já movimenta lobistas e políticos no governo Lula
item.description: Petrobras's recent oil discovery at the Amazon River mouth has already drawn lobbyists and politicians close to Lula's government, who are eyeing infrastructure contracts and royalties in Amapá and Belém. The scramble echoes the pre-salt boom and revives concerns about corruption risks similar to the Petrobras scandal exposed by Lava Jato. Planalto insiders say allies with presidential access are positioning themselves to profit from the new oil and gas supply chain.

item.title: Lula diz que governo não vai “matar 100 ou 200”, mas vai “prender”
item.description: At a campaign rally in Bangu alongside Eduardo Paes (PSD), Lula stated that his government's security policy will prioritize arresting criminals rather than lethal actions, and defended a Security Public PEC sent to Congress to create a Public Security Ministry and strengthen federal police forces. The remarks were an indirect reference to Operação Contenção from October 2025, which left 121 dead in Rio. Paes reinforced the PT-PSD alliance aimed at winning the 2026 election, while Lula thanked interim governor Ricardo Couto for the 'cleanup' following Cláudio Castro's resignation.

item.title: Tabata pede investigação ao TSE sobre filiação de Marçal ao PRTB
item.description: Deputy Tabata Amaral (PSB-SP) asked Brazil's Superior Electoral Court (TSE) to open a police investigation into a possible fraud in Pablo Marçal's affiliation with PRTB, after he switched from União Brasil past the legal deadline. The request is part of a lawsuit seeking the disqualification of Marçal's 2026 presidential candidacy, claiming he was still registered with União Brasil after the deadline and that his party membership was regularized retroactively.

item.title: Lula diz que é candidato mais uma vez para acabar com invisibilidade da população mais pobre
item.description: In his first campaign event in Rio de Janeiro, President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) framed his reelection bid as a project to bring the poorest population out of invisibility. Lula defended the continuity of social inclusion policies and the expansion of access to education as central pillars of his new campaign.

item.title: Lula e Flávio 'disputam' discurso sobre segurança em atos no Rio
item.description: President Lula and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro held simultaneous campaign rallies in Rio de Janeiro on Saturday (21), both vying for control of the public security narrative. The two presidential candidates presented contrasting approaches to the issue, marking another chapter in the 2026 race.

item.title: Em ato no Rio, Flávio Bolsonaro defende Bolsa Família e castração química para estupradores
item.description: At a rally in Maracanãzinho, the PL party officially launched Flávio Bolsonaro's presidential campaign and Douglas Ruas's bid for Rio's state government, focusing on public security. Flávio proposed classifying the PCC, Comando Vermelho, and militias as terrorist groups, advocated chemical castration for rapists, and acknowledged the importance of Bolsa Família. Douglas Ruas criticized Rio's mayor Eduardo Paes over the use of public funds for Carnival and major events.

item.title: Flávio busca unidade da direita em eventual segundo turno contra Lula
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) is trying to unify the right-wing to face Lula (PT) in a potential runoff, but struggles to consolidate votes from rival right-wing candidates. According to Datafolha, he would capture 60% of Zema's votes, 54% of Caiado's, and 48% of Renan Santos's, while the bases of these candidates are split almost evenly between him, Lula, and blank/null votes. To overcome the four-point gap against Lula, Flávio is avoiding controversies and reinforcing the anti-PT narrative, which also explains his potential absence at the Band debate.

item.title: Lula diz que “não tem preferência” entre EUA, China e Rússia
item.description: At a campaign rally in Bangu (Rio de Janeiro) alongside Eduardo Paes (PSD), President Lula stated he has no preference among the US, China, Russia, France, and the UK as Brazil's partners, emphasizing Brazil's rare earth mineral wealth and his goal to train qualified workers to exploit these resources without dependence on a single international partner. The event also reinforced the PT-PSD alliance in the state for the 2026 election.

item.title: "Terror vai acabar", diz Haddad sobre plataformas digitais nas escolas
item.description: Fernando Haddad (PT), running for governor of São Paulo, vowed to end the 'terror' faced by public school teachers by reviewing the use of digital platforms and screen time goals in schools. He also proposed doubling full-time enrollment slots, expanding CEUs to the interior and coastal regions, and creating student savings and technical education programs. Haddad took the opportunity to criticize Governor Tarcísio de Freitas' education management and stated that changes will begin on the first day of his administration.

item.title: STF retoma em setembro o julgamento da Lei da Ficha Limpa
item.description: The STF resumes on September 11 the virtual trial on the constitutionality of changes to the Clean Record Law made by Complementary Law 219/2025. The score is 2-0 against the changes that reduce ineligibility periods, which could benefit politicians such as Arruda, Cunha, and Garotinho.

item.title: Ao lado de Paes, Lula promete combater crime no Rio ‘sem pirotecnia’
item.description: President Lula held his first campaign event in Rio de Janeiro alongside gubernatorial candidate Eduardo Paes (PSD) at a rally in Bangu's Moça Bonita stadium. Lula endorsed the former mayor's candidacy and pledged to fight crime in the state 'without fireworks', signaling a focus on public security.

item.title: PL leva bonecos de papelão de Alexandre e Rebeca Ramagem para ato de Flávio Bolsonaro no Rio
item.description: The PL party brought cardboard cutouts of Alexandre and Rebeca Ramagem to a Flávio Bolsonaro rally at Maracanãzinho, where Douglas Ruas was officially launched as the party's candidate for Rio governor. Rebeca, who has been living in the United States since late 2025 following her husband's conviction in the coup plot case, is running her campaign for federal deputy remotely through social media.

item.title: Tarcísio diz gostaria de ver Lula e Flávio em debate
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos), running for reelection, said he would like to see President Lula (PT) and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) at the first 2026 presidential debate hosted by TV Bandeirantes, which both declined to attend. Tarcísio called their absence an 'electoral pragmatism' strategy and reaffirmed his support for Flávio's candidacy. A Datafolha poll shows Lula with 39% of voting intentions in the first round versus 33% for Flávio; in a potential runoff, Lula leads 47% to 43%.

item.title: Para Tarcísio, fechamento de lojas das Casas Bahia mostra que 'o Brasil não está indo bem'
item.description: Governor Tarcísio de Freitas warned about Brazil's difficult economic situation, citing the closure of around 300 Casas Bahia stores as evidence. He highlighted the negative impact of this downturn and the deteriorating scenario on the workers.

item.title: Lula volta a prometer recuperação da indústria da defesa no Brasil, mas diz não querer guerra
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), running for reelection, once again promised to revive Brazil's defense industry in a potential fourth term, expressing frustration with the country's external dependence in the sector. However, Lula stated he does not want war, signaling that the sector's strengthening would aim at sovereignty rather than military conflict.

item.title: Zema defende nova reforma da Previdência e admite aumentar tempo de contribuição
item.description: Presidential candidate Romeu Zema (Novo) defended a new pension reform during an agenda in São Paulo, proposing to increase contribution time for those entering the workforce, tied to gains in life expectancy. He also proposed an automatic adjustment mechanism, audits of the INSS, greater labor formalization, and work contracts based on hours actually worked.

item.title: Haddad: “O Datafolha está meio esquisito”
item.description: Fernando Haddad, PT candidate for the São Paulo state government, questioned the recent Datafolha poll results, calling the institute "a bit weird". The surveys show an advantage for the current governor Tarcísio de Freitas in the electoral race.

item.title: No Rio, Lula elogia Paes e Couto, e sai em defesa de Pedro Paulo após vaias: 'Nunca me fez nada e merece minha confiança'
item.description: Lula held his first campaign event in Rio de Janeiro, defending his alliance with Eduardo Paes and senator Pedro Paulo after boos from activists. He praised governor Ricardo Couto and pledged investments in security, education, defense, and healthcare.

item.title: Lula cobra resposta aos EUA e diz que recuperará indústria de defesa
item.description: Lula vowed to rebuild Brazil's defense industry and invest in clean energy and AI without provoking conflict, while criticizing Trump's military boasting. The speech in Rio also emphasized Brazil's vast borders and the pursuit of international respect.

item.title: Em campanha simultânea no Rio, Lula defende prender criminosos; e Flávio fala em ‘guerra’ ao crime
item.description: Lula promises to arrest criminals and return territories to the people, while Flávio Bolsonaro declares war on narcoterrorists starting in 2027. Both held simultaneous campaigns in Rio advocating public security policies.

item.title: Lula promete ‘devolver o território’ ao povo do Rio de Janeiro sem ‘pirotecnia’ na segurança
item.description: At a rally in Rio de Janeiro, President Lula pledged to reclaim territorial control without using aggressive methods, criticizing approaches based on 'fireworks'. He proposed creating a new Ministry of Public Security, contingent on the approval of the Security Constitutional Amendment, and praised interim governor Ricardo Couto and former mayor Eduardo Paes.

item.title: André do Prado se manifesta sobre investigação por campanha em igreja
item.description: André do Prado, running for Senate in São Paulo, responded after a request for investigation regarding a campaign event held in an evangelical church. He claimed he participated only as a guest in a faith context, without seeking votes. The complaint alleges misuse of a religious venue and potential electoral irregularities.

item.title: Caiado chama adversários de 'fujões' e 'amarelões' por provável ausência em debate presidencial
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado criticized the likely absence of opponents in presidential debates, calling them cowards and yellows. He claimed that candidates who do not participate are running, turning yellow, and chickening out, suggesting they avoid public discussion.

item.title: Lula e Renan têm mais voto por propostas, Flávio depende mais da rejeição
item.description: Datafolha polling on the 2026 presidential race shows Lula and Renan Cânbio rely more on vote-by-conviction based on proposals, while Flávio Bolsonaro depends more on voter rejection of opponents. A sizable voting bloc remains intent on preventing someone's victory, indicating persistent polarization.

item.title: ‘Olho por olho’, ‘dólar por dólar’: entenda como o Canadá pretende retaliar na mesma moeda as tarifas de Trump
item.description: Canada announced retaliatory 50% tariffs on US goods starting September 8, following the collapse of trade negotiations with Washington. Prime Minister Mark Carney justified the move as an equivalent response to the American tariff hike, targeting sectors including steel, dairy, and electronics. The decision marks the end of bilateral talks and intensifies the trade dispute between the two countries.

item.title: De colete à prova de balas, Renan Santos vai a comunidade em SP e promete programa de R$ 1,5 trilhão contra favelização
item.description: Renan Santos, presidential candidate from Missão, visited the Jardim Panorama community in São Paulo and proposed a slum-upgrading program with investments between R$1.3 and R$1.5 trillion. The plan includes housing renovation, property regularization, and expanded public services, without relocating residents. Funding will come from public and private sources, expense cuts, and tax exemptions.

item.title: Lula acena a religiosos e defende tirar o RJ das "páginas policiais"
item.description: Lula held his first campaign rally in Rio de Janeiro, focusing on public security and combating organized crime. He advocated moving the state from 'police pages' to 'political pages,' promising arrests without violence and returning territory to the people. The speech included strategic appeals to religiosity and references to God.

item.title: Lula promete “revolução energética” para sediar data centers
item.description: Lula promises an energy revolution focused on renewables to attract data centers, highlighting Brazil's potential in wind, solar, and green hydrogen. He advocates for the approval of the Redata tax exemption bill and mentioned other priorities like AI in Portuguese and public safety.

item.title: Lula diz que campanhas usarão IA porque rivais “não sabem a verdade”
item.description: Lula criticized the use of AI by his political opponents, claiming they lack commitment to truth and resort to technology to manipulate images and generate false content. He warned that the 2026 campaign will see extensive use of AI to distort reality, particularly targeting candidates like Eduardo Paes. The speech was delivered at a campaign rally in Rio de Janeiro, attended by allies and supporters of his re-election bid.

item.title: As metas ambiciosas do PL para as eleições à Câmara e ao Senado
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's PL party has set ambitious electoral targets for the upcoming elections: elect 105 federal deputies and increase its Senate caucus from 16 to 26 members. The strategy aims to strengthen the party in Congress and secure influence in the Legislative Branch, with potential plans to elect a Senate president if Bolsonaro wins the presidency.

item.title: Planos de governo de Lula e Flávio prometem seguro e crédito ao agro
item.description: Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro agree on expanding rural credit and insurance to combat 8.8% farm default rates. Lula emphasizes a record R$ 525 billion Safra Plan and catastrophic loss insurance, while Flávio proposes debt securitization and storage expansion. Both treat agribusiness as strategic, though Lula highlights family farming.

item.title: Lula volta a prometer Ministério da Segurança e reforça aliança com Paes em ato de campanha no Rio
item.description: Lula pledged to create a Ministry of Public Security during a campaign rally in Rio, reinforcing his alliance with Eduardo Paes. He advocated for a constitutional amendment to strengthen federal police forces, promising to reclaim territories from criminals and return them to the people.

item.title: Lula diz não querer guerra, mas investirá em Defesa: 'Não se metam conosco'
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva stated in Bangu, in the west zone of Rio de Janeiro, that he does not want war with any country, but intends to invest in Defense to prepare the country. In a warning tone, he declared 'Don't mess with us', signaling a stance of military strengthening.

item.title: Lula defende candidatura de Paes ao governo do Rio: 'É uma necessidade para o povo'
item.description: President Lula endorsed this Saturday the candidacy of former mayor Eduardo Paes for the governorship of Rio de Janeiro, calling it 'a necessity for the people'. The statement was made amid the 2026 electoral process, reinforcing the PT's support for an ally from PSD in the state of Rio.

item.title: Em evento na capital paulista, Tarcísio defende ampliação do metrô a novas regiões
item.description: São Paulo governor Tarcísio de Freitas stated that the state plans to expand transportation and specialized services in the capital. At an event alongside mayor Ricardo Nunes, he pledged to extend the metro to new areas and create more TEA Centers and Atypical Mother Houses.
